prerequisites: Sufficient knowledge of the subjects from Module 1 (Training Complements) and Module 2 (Instrumental)

learning_outcomes.text: Possess and understand knowledge that provides a basis or opportunity to be original in the development and/or application of ideas, often in a research context.
Students know how to apply the acquired knowledge and their problem-solving ability in new or little-known environments within broader (or multidisciplinary) contexts related to their field of study.

Students are able to integrate knowledge and face the complexity of forming judgments based on information that, being incomplete or limited, includes reflections on social and ethical responsibilities linked to the application of their knowledge and judgments.
Students know how to communicate their conclusions and the knowledge and ultimate reasons that support them to specialized and non-specialized audiences in a clear and unambiguous way.
Students possess the learning skills that allow them to continue studying in a way that will largely be self-directed or autonomous.
Write, scientifically interpret, and orally communicate, to specialized audiences, documents within the scope of the master's lines.
Develop the potential of information and communication technologies in industrial production.
Apply the knowledge obtained in the master's to achieve greater efficiency, effectiveness, reliability or safety in an industrial environment.
Manage, both theoretically and practically, the specific equipment for monitoring and control of automatic production systems.
Correctly apply the mandatory specifications, regulations and standards in the field of automatic industrial production systems.
Know the subjects and technologies that enable them to learn new methods and technologies, as well as provide them with sufficient versatility to adapt to new situations.
Develop optimal solutions for complex multidisciplinary problems in the field of automation and supervision of industrial production systems.
Use the acquired knowledge to maintain a critical and active attitude in the management of automation projects.
Analyze, design and build industrial computer applications.

Effectively use a systematic approach to the development of industrial process control logic, using standardized techniques for the analysis, design, implementation and documentation of the adopted solution.
Compare and evaluate commercial systems and technologies for process automation, selecting the most appropriate for a given application.
Design efficient automated systems using the most appropriate architecture for each case.
Apply modeling and programming techniques based on object orientation and available CASE tools for their implementation.
Qualify for the design and implementation of advanced automation systems, with special attention to distributed control systems.
Know and apply advanced instrumentation for its integration into automation systems.
Qualify for risk analysis, design and implementation of strategies for their reduction in automated machines and processes through the use of standardized functional safety techniques.

syllabus_topics: Modeling and programming techniques based on object orientation, components and CASE tools
Distributed control systems (DCS). Main characteristics. Fields of application. Selection criteria
DCS Architecture. Plant configuration, engineering and programming components. Monitoring, alarms, trends, historical data, diagnostics
Advanced integration of instrumentation in automation systems. Main devices. Standards and application tools
Functional safety. Regulations. Risk assessment and reduction. Design and validation of safe control systems. Safety controllers and networks. Integration into automation systems. Case studies

assessment_methods.method: Attendance, participation and submission of assignments associated with seminars (SEM)
Written evaluation test in the classroom (EVA)

assessment_rules: For ordinary and extraordinary calls, the final grade is calculated as: (SEM * 0.1) + (TR * 0.7) + (EV * 0.2). A minimum global score of 5 out of 10 for assignments (TR) and a minimum of 4 out of 10 for the written test (EV) are required to compensate with other tests. For differentiated evaluation, the final grade is: (TR * 0.6) + (EV * 0.4), with a minimum of 4 out of 10 in each of these two tests. Grades obtained in each test can be carried over between different calls within the same academic year.
